problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. Available containers are:

* Container 1: weight 28 tons, revenue 30 thousand dollars
* Container 2: weight 3 tons, revenue 56 thousand dollars
* Container 3: weight 24 tons, revenue 13 thousand dollars
* Container 4: weight 19 tons, revenue 168 thousand dollars
* Container 5: weight 4 tons, revenue 10 thousand dollars
* Container 6: weight 3 tons, revenue 32 thousand dollars
* Container 7: weight 10 tons, revenue 96 thousand dollars
* Container 8: weight 31 tons, revenue 51 thousand dollars
* Container 9: weight 38 tons, revenue 81 thousand dollars
* Container 10: weight 2 tons, revenue 297 thousand dollars
* Container 11: weight 9 tons, revenue 62 thousand dollars
* Container 12: weight 5 tons, revenue 43 thousand dollars
* Container 13: weight 39 tons, revenue 69 thousand dollars
* Container 14: weight 13 tons, revenue 61 thousand dollars
* Container 15: weight 32 tons, revenue 231 thousand dollars
* Container 16: weight 6 tons, revenue 68 thousand dollars
* Container 17: weight 31 tons, revenue 238 thousand dollars
* Container 18: weight 33 tons, revenue 96 thousand dollars
* Container 19: weight 35 tons, revenue 62 thousand dollars
* Container 20: weight 9 tons, revenue 200 thousand dollars

The vessel has a maximum cargo capacity of 261 tons. Determine which containers to load to maximize total revenue without exceeding this weight limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
